commands.name: commands
commands.summary: List this project's own CLI verbs (config commands: + plugin addCommand)
commands.description:
denext commands [--json] [--timeout <ms>] [--cwd <dir>]

  Imports denext.config.ts and runs every plugin setup() to discover the verbs the
  project contributes, then exits. A plugin that hangs or throws degrades to a notice
  (--json: `timedOut` / `error`); the exit code stays 0 either way.

  denext desktop package                 Build a distributable bundle (host OS: macOS or Linux)

  denext generate loading dashboard # app/dashboard/loading.tsx (root if no path)
  denext generate error dashboard   # app/dashboard/error.tsx (Client Component)

  denext generate component UserCard
  denext generate api users
  denext generate action createPost
  denext generate middleware        # middleware.ts (beside app/)

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Run the denext MCP server (stdio) so agents/IDEs can call denext's tooling
commands.description:
denext mcp                     # speak MCP over stdio (configure as an MCP server)
  denext mcp --disable rag,docs # expose fewer tools to trim the client's context

  Tools: denext_check_snippet, denext_import_map, denext_generate, denext_doctor,
  denext_codemod, denext_list_routes, denext_dev_logs, denext_render, denext_route_map,
  denext_search_docs, denext_index_codebase, denext_query_codebase, denext_find_definition,
  denext_find_references. Resources: denext://guide, denext://import-map.

  --disable takes a comma-separated list of groups (authoring, project, inspect, profile, dev, devtools, docs, rag) and/or tool
  names (with or without the denext_ prefix), e.g. --disable rag,docs or --disable render.

flags.name: disable
flags.description: Comma-separated groups (authoring, project, inspect, profile, dev, devtools, docs, rag) and/or tool names to hide

commands.name: mobile
commands.summary: Capacitor helpers (add: native capabilities; add-ota: over-the-air UI updates)
commands.description:
denext mobile add <capability...>
                                Add the Capacitor plugins behind denext/mobile's
                                capability functions, then `npx cap sync`
  denext mobile add deep-links --scheme myapp --domain app.example.com
                                Register a URL scheme and universal / app link domains
  denext mobile add push        Push notifications (entitlement, AppDelegate, permission)
  denext mobile add auth-session --scheme myapp
                                OAuth in a system browser sheet (openAuthSession)
  denext mobile add --list      List the capabilities and the plugins they install
  denext mobile add-ota [dir]   Install the DenextOta plugin into ios/ and android/

  add: finds the Capacitor project (the folder with capacitor.config.*: --dir when given,
  with no fallback, else the current directory), refuses when its @capacitor/core major
  is not the one the pinned plugins target, adds the packages with the package manager
  the nearest lockfile names (pnpm, npm, bun or yarn, looking up to the repository root
  for a workspace's; else a packageManager field; else npm), adds any Info.plist keys
  (never replacing yours) and Android permissions the capability needs, and runs
  `npx cap sync`. --dry-run prints the plan and changes nothing. Ship a new app binary
  afterwards.

  deep-links takes --scheme (CFBundleURLTypes + a VIEW intent filter) and --domain
  (applinks: in the entitlements + an autoVerify https intent filter); give several as
  a comma-separated list. The domains must also serve apple-app-site-association and
  assetlinks.json. push writes aps-environment (development) into the entitlements, the
  token forwarding into AppDelegate.swift and POST_NOTIFICATIONS into the manifest, and
  warns when android/app/google-services.json (FCM) is missing. A new entitlements file
  (ios/App/App/App.entitlements) must be selected in Xcode (Code Signing Entitlements);
  the steps left to do by hand are printed.

  auth-session has no npm package: it writes denext's DenextAuthSession plugin
  (ios/App/App/DenextAuthSessionPlugin.swift, an ASWebAuthenticationSession sheet, added to
  the App target; android dev/denext/authsession/*.java, a Custom Tab) and registers it
  through DenextBridgeViewController and MainActivity, which it shares with add-ota (either
  order works). --scheme registers the OAuth callback scheme as deep-links does; Android
  needs it to receive the redirect. No install or `cap sync` runs for it alone.

  iOS: writes DenextOtaPlugin.swift, DenextOtaStore.swift and DenextBridgeViewController.swift
  into ios/App/App/, adds them to the App target in project.pbxproj, and switches
  Main.storyboard and SceneDelegate to DenextBridgeViewController when they still use
  CAPBridgeViewController. Android: writes dev/denext/ota/*.java and calls
  DenextOta.prepare(this, bridgeBuilder) from a stock MainActivity. Customised files are
  left alone and listed as one-line manual steps. Safe to run again, and run it after every
  denext upgrade: unedited templates from an earlier denext are upgraded in place (ship a
  new app binary afterwards).

  --public-key ota.key.pub (from `denext ota keygen`) embeds the verifying key as Info.plist
  DenextOtaPublicKey and the dev.denext.ota.PUBLIC_KEY meta-data in AndroidManifest.xml
  (replacing an earlier one); the app then refuses any manifest not signed with its key.
  It exits non-zero when the key cannot be embedded on an installed platform, or an edited
  template was kept.

commands.name: ota
commands.summary: Over-the-air UI manifest for Capacitor apps
commands.description:
denext ota manifest out     Write out/_denext/ota.json (paths, SHA-256s, sizes, version)
  denext ota manifest out --required --notes "Fixes sign-in"
                              Also mark the UI required and attach release notes
  denext ota manifest out --sign ota.key
                              Also sign it (or set DENEXT_OTA_SIGNING_KEY to the PEM);
                              signing stamps --sequence (default: the Unix time) so apps
                              refuse an older release, and --min-native <build> refuses
                              app binaries older than that build number
  denext ota keygen ota.key   Write a P-256 signing key (0600) and ota.key.pub

  Run it after anything that changes the export (e.g. swapping brand icons in), and before
  `cap sync`, so the bundled UI and the served UI carry the right version. `spa.ota: true`
  makes `denext export` write it for you. `*.gz` files are never listed. `--required` and
  `--notes` feed the app's own update prompt (prepareUiUpdate in denext/mobile); they are
  not part of the version, but the signature covers them. An app whose binary embeds the
  public key (`denext mobile add-ota --public-key ota.key.pub`) refuses an unsigned or
  wrongly signed manifest; one without a key refuses plain http beyond loopback. Signing
  protects integrity only: over plain http the headers (bearer tokens) are visible on the
  network. `keygen --force` rotates the key, which breaks OTA for every installed binary
  that embeds the old public key.

flags.name: required
flags.description: Mark this UI as a required update (the app should not let users decline it)

flags.name: notes
flags.description: Release notes for the app's update prompt (at most 2000 characters)

flags.name: sign
flags.description: Sign the manifest with this PKCS#8 PEM key (default: $DENEXT_OTA_SIGNING_KEY, if set)

flags.name: sequence
flags.description: Release sequence (a non-negative integer that only grows; default when signing: the Unix time in seconds)

flags.name: min-native
flags.description: Refuse this UI on app binaries whose build number (CFBundleVersion / versionCode) is lower

flags.name: force
flags.description: keygen: replace existing key files (breaks OTA for binaries that embed the old public key)

positionals.name: path
positionals.description: manifest: the static export directory (e.g. out); keygen: the private key file

commands.name: patch
commands.summary: Patch npm packages — or denext itself (patches/*.patch)
commands.description:
denext patch create <package|denext> [dir]
  denext patch list [dir]
  denext patch delete <name|index> [dir]
  denext patch apply [dir]
  denext patch edit <package|denext> <file> [dir]

  create  diff the package's installed files (node_modules/<pkg>) — or denext's working
          copies (patches/.work/denext/) — against pristine → patches/<name>+<version>.patch
          (added and deleted files are recorded; a file over 2 MiB / 50k lines is skipped)
  list    the patches, indexed
  delete  remove a patch and undo it (npm files reverted, denext mapping dropped)
  apply   apply every patch now (dev/build/start/export do this at boot)
  edit    for denext: copy a framework file to patches/.work/denext/ to edit;
          for a package: print the installed file's path

  denext patch edit denext src/server/document.ts
  denext patch create denext
  denext patch create left-pad
  denext patch delete 2

positionals.name: name
positionals.description: Package name, `denext`, or (delete) a list index

commands.name: plugin
commands.description:
denext plugin add <pkg> [dir]
  denext plugin remove <pkg> [dir]
  denext plugin list [dir]

  add     adds the dependency (deno add) and wires the plugin into denext.config.ts
  remove  unwires the plugin from denext.config.ts and drops the dependency
  list    show the plugins wired into denext.config.ts

  denext plugin add @denext/htmx
  denext plugin remove @denext/htmx
  denext plugin list
  denext plugin add my-plugin --export configureMyPlugin

commands.name: test
commands.description:
Forwards to `deno test -A`. Extra args/paths pass through:
  denext test                  Run every test
  denext test --watch          Re-run on change (deno test --watch)
  denext test --coverage=cov   Collect coverage, then `deno coverage cov`
  denext test --filter Auth    Forward deno test flags
  denext test routes/          Restrict to a path

commands.name: ui
commands.summary: Open the project management UI in a browser (loopback only)
commands.description:
denext ui                    Serve the UI for the current project and open it
  denext ui ./my-app --port 6000   That exact port, or a clear error if it is taken
  denext ui --read-only        Browse without offering any write
  denext ui --offline          Keep the UI and the processes it starts off the network
  denext ui --no-open --json   Print { url, port, token } and keep serving

  The UI binds and is opened at 127.0.0.1 only (never localhost, whose cookies every
  local server shares). The printed URL carries a per-launch 256-bit token that is
  exchanged ONCE for an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie holding a separate, freshly
  minted secret — the query token is then refused, so a copied link cannot open a
  second session. Every mutation additionally needs a same-origin Origin and a CSRF
  token derived from the cookie.
  Note: with --open, the token is visible in the browser-launcher's argv on this machine.

flags.name: port
flags.description: Port to listen on (default 5177, which falls forward when busy; an explicit --port is required exactly, and 0 picks a free one)

flags.name: offline
flags.description: Never reach the network: no JSR search; denext verbs and doctor run with --deny-net --cached-only, deno install with --cached-only; deno task, denext dev and plugin add/remove are refused (combines with --read-only)

flags.name: token
flags.description: Use this session token instead of minting one (at least 22 characters)

flags.name: ui-dev
flags.description: Internal: watch src/ui and reload open pages on change

commands.name: update
commands.description:
Forwards to `deno outdated --update`. Pass package names to scope it,
or `--latest` to cross semver ranges.

projectCommands.note: A project can add its own verbs — `commands: [{ name, summary, run }]` in denext.config.ts, or a plugin's `addCommand`. They are resolved from the project's config, so they are not listed here. `denext --help` lists only the built-in verbs — it never imports the project — and inside a denext project it ends with "Project verbs: run `denext commands` (they are also in shell completions)." `denext commands` and `denext completions <shell>` load them (under a 1.5 s budget). A built-in verb always wins a name collision.
